steps.description: Load the raw count matrix (12000 genes x 2 samples: treated, control) and metadata. Build a DESeqDataSet with design ~condition (2 levels: treated vs control). steps.description: From the 12000-gene raw count matrix, keep genes with at least 10 counts in at least 1 sample (the smallest group size here is 1 sample per group). acceptance_criteria: Genes filtered using >=10 counts in >=1 sample (smallest group size)

steps.description: Using the normalized counts from T1S2, compute a descriptive log2 fold change per gene as log2((normalized_count_treated + pseudocount) / (normalized_count_control + pseudocount)), with pseudocount=1. Do NOT run DESeq()/nbinomWaldTest or any dispersion-based inferential test: with one sample per group there is no within-group variance to estimate a dispersion from, so a p-value would have no statistical basis (per the design flag for zero-replicate groups). Output a full gene table with: gene symbol, normalized counts (both samples), raw counts (both samples), descriptive log2FC, and rank by |log2FC| descending. State explicitly in the output that these are descriptive effect sizes only, not statistically tested differential expression calls, and name the replicated design (e.g., >=3 biological replicates per group) that would support an inferential DESeq2/edgeR test.
acceptance_criteria: No p-values or FDR-adjusted values reported anywhere in this step's output
Full gene table (post-filter gene count) with descriptive log2FC, raw and normalized counts per sample
Explicit statement that the design lacks replication and what design would support inference
Genes ranked by absolute descriptive log2FC

steps.description: From T1S3's ranked gene table, select the top genes by |descriptive log2FC| (state the count and cutoff used, e.g. top 200 genes by absolute log2FC, since there is no significance threshold available in this design) as the query gene list. Set the universe/background to all genes that passed the low-count filter in T1S2 (the tested genes), not the whole genome. Run over-representation analysis (hypergeometric test, e.g. clusterProfiler::enricher) against the MSigDB Hallmark human gene sets (50 sets) first, then against the Reactome human gene sets (filtered to Homo sapiens from the combined Reactome GMT using the Reactome pathway index) as a follow-up collection. Reactome ORA run as a second pass, human-filtered
Gene set size window 15-500 applied after intersecting with the universe

plan.title: Liver treated vs control DE — descriptive, no replicates
plan.analytical_narrative: The dataset is a single treated liver sample vs a single control liver sample (1v1, no biological replicates), raw salmon gene counts for 12000 genes across 3 columns (gene symbol + 2 samples). With one sample per group there is no within-group variance to estimate a dispersion from, so an inferential DE test (Wald/LRT with p-values) has no statistical basis — this is exactly the design the knowledge service flags (R-0003) as requiring descriptive-only treatment. The plan therefore: (1) confirms sample structure and library size via DESeq2 QC utilities even though PCA/clustering is uninformative with n=1 per group, (2) filters low-count genes, (3) computes DESeq2 median-of-ratios size factors and normalized counts, (4) reports descriptive (unshrunk, no-test) log2 fold changes between the two samples using normalized counts, explicitly refusing any p-value, (5) runs over-representation enrichment (not preranked GSEA, per the knowledge-service ruling for this situation) using the genes with the largest descriptive fold changes against an explicit tested-gene universe, over MSigDB Hallmark and then Reactome human gene sets, and (6) produces a report stating the design limitation, all thresholds, package versions, and gene set collection versions. No claim of statistical significance is made anywhere in the plan.
